headline: Bring eGauge energy readings into Home Assistant
intro: Connect to an eGauge monitor on your local network with its host, username, and password. Home Assistant checks the device identity and register permissions, then polls its registers for electrical readings.
highlights: Setup checks the monitor's serial number and hostname; the serial number prevents adding the same device twice.
Choose whether to use SSL and verify its certificate. Certificate verification is off by default because eGauge devices use a self-signed certificate unless a custom one is installed.
Home Assistant creates sensors for supported power, energy, voltage, and current registers, and refreshes measurements and counters every 30 seconds.

flow.title: Connect and read registers
stages: Enter the device host and credentials
Validate access and identify the monitor
Poll supported electrical registers every 30 seconds
